candidates.source_name: Bankart d.o.o. — corporate site (Podjetje / company profile)
candidates.why_relevant: Bankart is the domestic card switch/processor owned by Slovenian banks; its own pages state operating scale (card volumes, POS/ATM networks managed, SEPA volumes) and corporate/ownership structure. This is the ecosystem core with no banking-report equivalent.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Periodic HTML scrape/diff of key pages (podjetje, izdajateljstvo, sprejemanje kartic, placilni-sistemi-in-storitve); quarterly cadence.
queries_used: Bankart procesiranje kartic transakcije statistika Slovenija

candidates.source_name: Bankart d.o.o. — annual reports (Letno poročilo) PDFs
candidates.why_relevant: Audited annual reports of the domestic processor contain revenue, transaction/processing volumes, number of cards and terminals processed, ownership shares of member banks, and business commentary on the SI card market. The 2019 report explicitly compares Bankart-processed POS count against Bank of Slovenia totals — a rare direct market-share datapoint.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl /wp-content/uploads/ year folders for 'Letno-poroc*' PDFs annually (published ~Apr-Aug); PDF text extraction. Cross-check against AJPES filing.
queries_used: Bankart d.o.o. Ljubljana letno poročilo kartično poslovanje
bankart.si "letno poročilo" 2024 OR 2023 pdf

candidates.source_name: Banka Slovenije — Poravnava kartic (card settlement system page)
candidates.why_relevant: Central bank description of the domestic card clearing/settlement system operated by Bankart (Mastercard, Karanto, BA/Maestro at POS and ATMs) and its settlement in TARGET2-Slovenija. Authoritative on which schemes/rails clear domestically and who operates them.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: HTML scrape + change detection; semi-annual.
queries_used: bsi.si poravnava kartic Bankart Activa plačilni sistem nadzor

candidates.source_name: Banka Slovenije — Upravljavci plačilnih sistemov (register of payment system operators)
candidates.why_relevant: Authoritative register naming every licensed payment-system operator in SI (Bankart, Activa/Intesa-operated system, etc.). Best pointer for keeping the actor map of switches/schemes current, and for detecting entries/exits.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scrape register table quarterly; diff entity list. Pair with 'Dovoljenja Banke Slovenije' licence-decision page.
queries_used: bsi.si poravnava kartic Bankart Activa plačilni sistem nadzor

candidates.source_name: Banka Slovenije — Poročanje podatkov statistike plačil (payment statistics reporting)
candidates.why_relevant: Defines the reporting obligation and templates under which acquirers/processors/issuers must submit card, ATM and POS data — reveals exactly which variables exist in the SI payments dataset and therefore what can ever be asked for.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Download reporting instructions/templates on change; annual review.
queries_used: Banka Slovenije statistika plačilnih kartic bankomati POS terminali

candidates.source_name: Banka Slovenije — Statistična poročila / Finančne institucije in trgi
candidates.why_relevant: Publishes the semi-annual SI payment/card statistics releases (cards issued by type, ATM count and contactless share, POS terminal count and growth) — the national denominator against which scheme/processor claims are benchmarked.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monitor publication index; download releases and any XLSX series semi-annually.
queries_used: Banka Slovenije statistika plačilnih kartic bankomati POS terminali

candidates.source_name: ECB Data Portal — PCP dataset (card payments & cash withdrawals, incl. fraud), SI country tables
candidates.why_relevant: Harmonised, machine-readable country-level card/ATM/POS series for Slovenia, comparable across the euro area; also documents the multi-acquiring double-counting caveat that matters when reading SI terminal counts.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: SDMX/REST pull of PCP and PAY datasets filtered REF_AREA=SI; semi-annual after each release.
queries_used: ECB payments statistics Slovenia card payments acquirers data warehouse

candidates.source_name: ECB payments statistics press releases (half-yearly)
candidates.why_relevant: Narrative release accompanying each payments-statistics vintage; gives euro-area context and flags methodology changes affecting the SI series.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: RSS/index monitoring of the paysec release folder, semi-annual.
queries_used: ECB payments statistics Slovenia card payments acquirers data warehouse

candidates.source_name: Worldline — Indicative Card Scheme Fee Rates, Slovenia (PDF)
candidates.why_relevant: Country-specific acquirer disclosure of Visa/Mastercard scheme fees applied in Slovenia, with a domestic-transaction definition. Rare hard pricing evidence for the SI acquiring stack; a versioned PDF that can be diffed over time.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Fetch the stable /content/dam/ PDF quarterly; hash-diff and extract fee tables. Watch for date-stamped supersessions.
queries_used: Visa interchange fee rates Europe Slovenia domestic rates PDF

candidates.source_name: Mastercard Slovenija — Medfranšizne stopnje in provizije (interchange)
candidates.why_relevant: Scheme's own Slovenian-language interchange disclosure page; the entry point to SI-applicable interchange rate tables and qualification criteria mandated by the EU Interchange Fee Regulation.
candidates.access_status: open (rate tables often behind linked PDFs)
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scrape page and follow linked rate-table PDFs; semi-annual (rates typically revised ~April/October).
queries_used: Visa Mastercard medbančna provizija interchange Slovenija objava
Mastercard Slovenija medfranšizne stopnje provizije interchange site:mastercard.si

candidates.source_name: Visa Europe — Fees and interchange (country rate tables)
candidates.why_relevant: Visa's European interchange hub linking per-country PDFs of intra-EEA/domestic interchange rates; the counterpart to the Mastercard SI disclosure and the second half of scheme-side pricing evidence.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scrape hub page for linked country PDFs, filter Slovenia; semi-annual diff. Note there is also a Slovenian-language Visa site (visa.si) to check for SI-specific pages.
queries_used: Visa interchange fee rates Europe Slovenia domestic rates PDF

candidates.source_name: Nexi Slovenija d.o.o. (formerly Nets CEE / Intesa Sanpaolo Card) — company records
candidates.why_relevant: Business-register aggregator record for the SI arm of the Nexi processing group (activity code 63.100, parent Nexi Croatia d.o.o. za kartično poslovanje). Gives legal identity, ownership chain, headcount and filed financials for the largest international processor present in SI.
candidates.access_status: partially paywalled (headline data free, full reports paid)
candidates.legal_status: commercial redistribution of public AJPES filings — check ToS before bulk scraping
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Manual/low-frequency lookup for entity changes; prefer AJPES as the primary filing source for financial statements.
queries_used: Nexi Slovenija acquiring pridobitelj kartično poslovanje trgovci

candidates.source_name: AJPES — Slovenian business register & annual report repository (JOLP)
candidates.why_relevant: Statutory filings of Bankart, Nexi Slovenija, Sparkasse Pay and any acquirer/processor entity: audited financial statements, ownership and activity codes. Primary source behind every commercial aggregator; the reliable long-term backbone for tracking processor economics.
candidates.access_status: open with search UI; some services require registration
candidates.legal_status: public register; reuse conditions apply to bulk extraction
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Annual entity-by-entity lookup (JOLP) for the cell's actor list; store PDFs/XBRL. Confirm bulk-access terms before automating.
candidates.discovered_via_method: inference from first principles (who must file) + aggregator snowball
queries_used: Bankart d.o.o. Ljubljana letno poročilo kartično poslovanje

candidates.source_name: Sparkasse Pay d.o.o. — Diners Club Slovenija issuer site
candidates.why_relevant: The legacy Diners Club brand in Slovenia is now issued by Sparkasse Pay d.o.o. (Ameriška ulica 2, Ljubljana) as Diners Club–Mastercard products. Tracks the fate of a legacy three-party scheme brand, its merchant-acceptance network and consumer-credit intermediation disclosures.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scrape product/tariff and 'prodajna mesta' pages semi-annually; note the parallel dinersclub.si domain serving the same content.
queries_used: Activa Diners Club kartice Slovenija izdajatelj

candidates.source_name: Banka Intesa Sanpaolo (SI) — Activa card system operator & product disclosures
candidates.why_relevant: The Activa brand and card system (created 1992 at Banka Koper) is operated by Banka Intesa Sanpaolo, which performs the clearing while Bank of Slovenia settles daily via TARGET2-Slovenija. The bank's product key-information sheets carry Activa Mastercard fees and terms — the surviving commercial trace of the legacy domestic scheme.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Track the 'ključne informacije' product PDFs and the annual report (letno poročilo) for Activa-system commentary; annual + on-change.
queries_used: "Activa" kartica Slovenija sistem znamka bankart zgodovina

candidates.source_name: Wikipedija (sl) — Sistem Activa
candidates.why_relevant: Compact Slovenian-language history and structure of the Activa card system (founded 1992 at Banka Koper; clearing by Intesa Sanpaolo, settlement by Banka Slovenije via TARGET2-Slovenija; covers Mastercard/Visa/Activa/Maestro/Cirrus/Visa Electron). Useful for glossary and actor-map seeding, not as evidence.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: One-off extraction for glossary/actor map; re-check annually. Always corroborate claims against BSI or issuer sources.
queries_used: "Activa" kartica Slovenija sistem znamka bankart zgodovina

candidates.source_name: Banka Slovenije — Nacionalni svet za plačila, meeting materials
candidates.why_relevant: The National Payments Council brings together the central bank, banks, Bankart and merchant/consumer bodies; published session materials are one of the few places where SI card-acceptance costs, instant payments and scheme developments are discussed with slides and numbers.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Poll the gradiva index quarterly; download new agenda/presentation PDFs and extract charts.
queries_used: bsi.si poravnava kartic Bankart Activa plačilni sistem nadzor

candidates.source_name: Kansas City Fed — Credit and Debit Card Interchange Fees in Various Countries (annual update)
candidates.why_relevant: Annual cross-country compendium that includes Slovenia's interchange caps/regime; a stable, citable secondary benchmark when scheme PDFs are hard to pin down, and a good consistency check on IFR implementation.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Fetch the August update annually; extract the Slovenia row.
queries_used: Visa interchange fee rates Europe Slovenia domestic rates PDF

candidates.source_name: Worldline Global — merchant acquiring / financial-institution processing pages and press releases
candidates.why_relevant: Worldline is an active acquirer/processor in Slovenia (e.g. Bank Transfer by Worldline available to SI merchants since Aug 2024) and its press releases are the main public signal of country-level product launches and bank outsourcing deals in the SI processing stack.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monitor the media-relations press-release feed, filter for Slovenia/SEE; quarterly.
queries_used: Worldline Slovenia payment acquiring merchant services

candidates.source_name: Academic theses repository (CEK, Univerza v Ljubljani, Ekonomska fakulteta)
candidates.why_relevant: Slovenian economics theses on the card market frequently contain otherwise-unpublished detail on Activa/Bankart volumes, issuer shares and merchant fees, obtained directly from banks. A useful archive of historical series that no longer exist publicly.

candidates.source_name: Delo / Finance — Slovenian business press coverage of interchange and card fees
candidates.why_relevant: National business press is where SI-specific interchange/MDR disputes, Bankart ownership changes and acquirer entries surface first, often quoting figures not otherwise published. The archived Delo piece on IFR caps and Slovenia is an example of usable local commentary.

negative_findings.description: Searches for Bankart annual reports newer than FY2020 returned only the 2019 and 2020 PDFs on bankart.si; no 2023/2024 'letno poročilo' surfaced in search results.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only /wp-content/uploads/2020/04/ (FY2019) and /wp-content/uploads/2021/08/ (FY2020) PDFs located. Recent years may exist but be unindexed, differently named, or filed only with AJPES. Not verified as absent.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The most recent processor-side volume and market-share data may only be reachable via AJPES filings rather than the company website, which changes the collection method.

negative_findings.description: No Slovenia-specific published transaction volume or market-share dataset was found from Visa or Mastercard themselves.
negative_findings.result_summary: Scheme sites expose interchange/fee disclosures for SI, but no country transaction statistics. Country-level card volumes appear only via Banka Slovenije and the ECB.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Scheme-side SI volumes must be triangulated from central-bank/ECB data plus processor reports; do not expect a scheme-published SI volume series.

negative_findings.description: The relationship between the legacy 'Activa' brand and current issuance is only partially documented in public sources.
negative_findings.result_summary: Confirmed: Activa system created 1992 at Banka Koper, operated by Banka Intesa Sanpaolo, settled by Banka Slovenije; Activa Mastercard products still marketed. Not confirmed: whether the Activa clearing system is still live as a separate payment system or has been folded into scheme processing.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Determines whether Activa remains a distinct data-generating rail worth tracking, or is now only a consumer brand.

negative_findings.description: No Slovenian-language Worldline or Nexi country site with SI merchant/acquirer disclosures was located.
negative_findings.result_summary: Worldline material for SI is English (global domain); Nexi's regional SI-relevant content appears via nexi.hr (Croatian). Nexi Slovenija d.o.o. has no evident customer-facing SI website in search results.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Local-language monitoring for these two processors will have to rely on business registers and press rather than their own SI-language sites.

negative_findings.description: No Slovenian public registry of merchant service charges (MDR) per acquirer was found.
negative_findings.result_summary: IFR Art. 12 requires acquirers to disclose MDR to merchants individually, but no aggregated SI public dataset surfaced. Only Worldline's SI scheme-fee PDF and scheme interchange tables are public.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Acquiring-price intelligence for SI will require assembling individual acquirer tariff documents (bank price lists), not a central source.

brief: Slovenia's card ecosystem has an unusually concentrated data core: Bankart d.o.o., the bank-owned domestic switch and processor, both creates the transaction data and discloses scale figures on its site and in its annual reports, while Banka Slovenije publishes the national denominators (cards, ATMs, POS terminals) and describes the Poravnava kartic settlement system Bankart operates. Scheme-side, the useful public material is pricing rather than volume: Mastercard's Slovenian-language 'medfranšizne stopnje' disclosure, Visa Europe's country interchange tables, and Worldline's Slovenia scheme-fee PDF; neither scheme publishes SI transaction volumes, so those must come from the ECB PCP dataset and BSI. Legacy brands remain live but transformed — Activa, created in 1992 at Banka Koper, is operated by Banka Intesa Sanpaolo and survives as Activa Mastercard products, while Diners Club Slovenija is now issued by Sparkasse Pay d.o.o. The main open gaps are per-acquirer merchant tariffs (the only public MDR evidence in SI), Bankart's post-2020 annual reports, and independent ATM operators.
